m.h: Note that if the number of periods between the day you start saving and the date of your goal is fractional, the number of periods is rounded up.
For the sake of simplicity, we suppose that your birthday is today.
Use this field if you already have some savings.
Annual nominal interest rate or annual rate of return.
The frequency interest is added to the principal balance of your savings, or, in other words, how often the earned return or interest is reinvested.
The annual rate of inflation. Note, that you can set a negative value if you expect a fall in the general price level during the set interval, representing deflationary pressures.
The percentage growth rate of your additional periodic contribution over a year.

The percentage growth rate of your periodic contributions. Note, that periodic and annual growth rates are linked together: if you set one, the other will be calculated according to the regularity of your additional deposit.

c: payment_per_period > 0 and Infl == 0
You need to put aside {{payment_per_period.monetaryValue}} each {{period_name.uiValue}} to reach your savings goal.
payment_per_period > 0 and Infl > 0
You need to put aside {{payment_per_period.monetaryValue}} each {{period_name.uiValue}} to reach your savings goal in the real, inflation-adjusted term.
Infl == 0 and InDep == 0
The sum of your {{period_name2.uiValue}} savings will be {{sum_savings.monetaryValue}}, with a total return of {{total_return.monetaryValue}}.
Infl == 0 and InDep != 0
The sum of your {{period_name2.uiValue}} savings with the initial balance will be {{sum_savings_plus_initial.monetaryValue}}, with a total return of {{total_return.monetaryValue}}.
Infl != 0 and InDep == 0

The final nominal value (without inflation adjustment) of your savings will be {{final_nom_value.monetaryValue}}. The sum of your {{period_name2.uiValue}} savings will be {{sum_savings.monetaryValue}}.
Infl != 0 and InDep != 0

The final nominal value (without inflation adjustment) of your savings will be {{final_nom_value.monetaryValue}}. The sum of your {{period_name2.uiValue}} savings with the initial balance will be {{sum_savings_plus_initial.monetaryValue}}.
Infl != 0 and real_return >= 0
You will gain a {{total_return.monetaryValue}} return in nominal terms, which is {{real_return.monetaryValue}} in real, inflation-adjusted terms.
Infl != 0 and real_return < 0

You will gain {{total_return.monetaryValue}} in nominal terms, which does not cover the purchasing power loss caused by inflation. It means that if you take inflation into account, you have lost {{real_return_abs.monetaryValue}}.

name: Savings plan
title: Savings Plan Calculator
desc: Use the savings plan calculator to create a money-saving plan and estimate how much money you could save by following different money-saving challenges.

m.l: I'd like to plan with a...

m.h: You can also set a negative value here if you would like to decrease the saving amount periodically.

c: VarMode == 1 or VarMode == 3
Your final balance will be {{finalBalance.monetaryValue}}.
VarMode == 2 and DepAdd == 0  and myPlan == 1
You need to put aside {{periodicDeposit.monetaryValue}} on each day to accomplish your plan.
VarMode == 2 and DepAdd == 0 and myPlan == 2
You need to put aside {{periodicDeposit.monetaryValue}} on each week to accomplish your plan.
VarMode == 2 and DepAdd == 0 and myPlan == 3
You need to put aside {{periodicDeposit.monetaryValue}} on every second week to accomplish your plan.
VarMode == 2 and DepAdd == 0 and myPlan == 4
You need to put aside {{periodicDeposit.monetaryValue}} on each month to accomplish your plan.
DepFirst > 0 and VarMode == 2 and DepAdd > 0
You need to begin your savings with {{initialDeposit.monetaryValue}} and increase it each period to accomplish your plan.
DepFirst <= 0 and VarMode == 2 and DepAdd > 0
Please either lower the deposit for the repeated increase or set a higher value for your target as with the given values the first deposit is negative.
periodicDeposit < 0

desc: Use the savings withdrawal calculator to determine how long your money will last or how much money you can withdraw from your savings through a specific period.

opts: how long will my money last?

m.h: The current balance of your savings.
If you choose a future date, your current balance stated above will increase according to the average interest rate.
The amount you are planning to withdraw monthly.
The average interest rate or APY on your savings.

opts: At the end of the month
At the beginning of the month

m.h: The percentage growth rate of your withdrawals over a year.

The percentage growth rate of the monthly withdrawals. Note, that periodic and annual growth rates are linked together: if you set one, the other will be calculated according to annuity frequency. Available only at fixed length annuity.
Set an amount if you want to have some money left at the end of the withdrawal period.

c: Subject == 2
Your savings will last for {{last_for_years.value}} year(s) and {{last_for_months.value}} month(s) from the first day of withdrawal.
Subject == 2 and bal_last_withdrawal > 0
After withdrawing for {{last_for_years.value}} year(s) and {{last_for_months.value}} month(s), you will have {{bal_last_withdrawal.monetaryValue}}.
Subject == 2 and isNaN(last_for_years)
The length of withdrawal is infinite since the monthly interest earned exceeds the withdrawal amount.
Subject == 1 and Type == 0
You can withdraw {{withdrawal_amount.monetaryValue}} at the end of each month to deplete your savings entirely.
Subject == 1 and Type == 1
You can withdraw {{withdrawal_amount.monetaryValue}} at the beginning of each month to deplete your savings entirely.
Subject == 3
You will have {{remaining_amount.monetaryValue}} after the set length of withdrawals.

m.h: The expected average inflation rate before retirement.
Interval between the regular withdrawals.

Subject == 3 and g == 0

You can withdraw {{withdrawal.monetaryValue}} initially and increase it gradually to reach the final balance.
Subject == 3 and g < 0

You can withdraw the given amount periodically without receiving any return on your investment.

name: TDS interest
title: TDS Interest Calculator
desc: Use the TDS interest calculator to estimate interest charges on late payments, late deductions, or interest on late filing of a TDS return.

c: subject == 1
(Section 201(1A)) If TDS is not deducted on time, interest is charged at 1% per month (or part of a month). Calculated from the due date of deduction to the actual deduction date.
subject == 2
(Section 201(1A)) If TDS is deducted but not deposited on time, interest is charged at 1.5% per month (or part of a month). Calculated from the date of deduction to the actual deposit date.
subject == 3
(Section 234E) This is a penalty for not filing the TDS return on time. Charged at ₹200 per day from the due date until the return is filed. Maximum penalty cannot exceed the TDS amount.

m.h: The date credit is given to the party or when the dues are actually paid, whichever is earlier.
The given year refers to the financial year that begins in that year. For example, the year 2026 refers to the financial year that runs from 1st April 2025 until 31st March 2026.
The actual date of filing the return.

c: subject == 1 and dateTrans == dateDed
TDS was deducted on the day when the transaction was made.
subject == 1 and dateTrans > dateDed
The transaction date can't be later than the deduction date.
subject == 1 and tdsInterest > 0
The interest on the late deduction, which needs to be paid before the TDS return is filed, is ₹{{tdsInterest.formattedValue}}.
subject == 2 and dateDed > datePmt
The deduction date can't be later than the payment date.
subject == 2 and tdsInterest > 0
The interest on late payment, which needs to be paid before the TDS return is filed, is ₹{{tdsInterest.formattedValue}}.
subject == 3 and tdsInterest > 0 and tdsInterest < tax
The fee on late filing is ₹{{tdsInterest.formattedValue}}.
subject == 3 and tdsInterest == tax
The amount of the fee can't exceed the tax amount — the fee on late filing is ₹{{tdsInterest.formattedValue}}.
subject == 2 and tdsInterest == 0 and dateDed <= datePmt
You are still within the deadline. You must pay the TDS by {{dueDate.formattedValue}} to avoid interest charges.
subject == 3 and tdsInterest == 0
You are still within the deadline. You must file the TDS by {{dueDate.formattedValue}} to avoid fees.

name: VA loan
title: VA Loan Calculator
desc: VA loan calculator is a comprehensive tool for evaluating a VA loan's monthly mortgage payment, the debt-to-income ratio that qualifies you for the loan, the total cost of the loan, and the amount of VA loan entitlement guaranteed on the loan.

m.l: Is this your first VA loan?

m.h: County loan limits currently range from $548,250 to $822,375.
How much of your entitlement did you use on your previous VA loan?
If you make a down payment, you will pay less in funding fees.
VA loan rates typical range from 2.25% to 4%.

m.l: Are you exempted from paying Funding fees?
m.h: If you are not sure, read the Are you exempted from funding fees? section in the text.
Maximum guaranty the VA will offer for this loan based on your VA entitlement.
If the VA is not offering the maximum 25% guaranty to your lender, you may be required to pay the difference to qualify for the loan.
Total estimated cost of originating and paying off the loan, taxes and insurance.
Monthly principal and interest payment (PI).
Estimated monthly payment with taxes and homeowner insurance costs (PITI).

c: Disclaimer: The VA loan calculator provide an estimate of the payment amount based on the data provided. The actual payment may differ depending on the lender, county taxes, and home insurance charge.

m.h: Estimated monthly expenses.
Debt-to-income ratio that determines the percentage of income spent on paying off the loan.

c: dti_ratio > 0.49
❗ Your DTI is extremely dangerous. You should consider purchasing a cheaper home.
dti_ratio <= 0.49
⚠️ Your DTI is dangerous. You should consider reducing your expenses.
dti_ratio <= 0.41
👋 Your DTI is satisfactory. You should qualify for this loan.
dti_ratio <= 0.36
👍 Your DTI is good. You qualify for this loan.
dti_ratio <= 0.2
💪 Your DTI is excellent. You easily qualify for this loan.

eq.formula: net_monthly_payment = loan_amount * interest_rate_per_month * ((1 + interest_rate_per_month) ^ number_of_payments) / ((1 + interest_rate_per_month) ^ (number_of_payments) - 1)
